title: Render svg preview images in File Explorer is too slow
author: sebasav182

status.label: Performance design investigation queued
status.detail: The report matches the current per-thumbnail synchronous process/render handoff, but profiling and implementation-grade design are still needed.

next_action.label: Develop SVG thumbnail performance design
next_action.reason: Profile the provider and design bounded reuse/concurrency without premature approval.

judgment.rationale: The issue gives a clear workload and severe per-item latency, while source reveals a plausible high-cost ownership path suitable for focused design investigation.
evidence: A first visit to a directory with at least 50 SVG files renders thumbnails one at a time at roughly 4–5 seconds each.
SvgThumbnailProvider::GetThumbnail writes each stream to a temporary SVG, starts PowerToys.SvgThumbnailProvider.exe, waits synchronously with an infinite timeout, then loads a temporary BMP.
The provider has output-correctness tests but the inspected path has no throughput or bounded-time test.
judgment.recommended_action: Develop a profiled implementation-grade design covering process reuse or in-process rendering, timeout/cancellation, Shell concurrency, cache behavior, and representative SVG tests.

issue_context.summary: SVG thumbnail generation is extremely slow for a folder of many files, and the provider pays a synchronous external-process and temporary-file handoff for each thumbnail.
known_information: The author supplied version, Windows build, workload size, observed latency, and screenshot.
The delay occurs on the first directory visit while thumbnails are generated.
The native shell provider waits for a managed renderer process per request.
Recent history hardened cleanup/decoding but does not establish a throughput fix.
inferences: Per-request process startup and serialization may contribute materially, but profiling is needed before calling it root cause.
Explorer scheduling may also affect visible serialization, so blind parallelism could create COM or resource problems.
issue_context.analysis: The source cost center is concrete enough for design work, not approve_design. The design must measure startup/render/cache costs and choose a safe lifetime/concurrency strategy compatible with Explorer.
initial_investigation: Located SVG thumbnail correctness tests under UnitTests-SvgThumbnailProvider.
Reviewed cleanup/decoding and provider-combination history; no linked issue-specific fix PR exists.

information_gaps.information: A representative profile on current stable/main separating startup, rendering, and Explorer scheduling.
information_gaps.why_needed: The design must target the dominant cost and avoid unsafe speculative parallelism.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use provider logs/profiling with a representative 50-file SVG directory during full design investigation.
